others.method: CLI: wall time of the process and /usr/bin/time -l's maximum RSS, after one unmeasured run (page cache warm); default locale. less: a pseudo-terminal from script(1); ms until the file's first line is written, and after G until its last line is.

binary.method: file size of target/<profile>/strata; stripped = `strip -o` of the release binary; release-small = opt-level s, fat LTO, 1 codegen unit, strip (ashlar's profile, passed with --config)

idle.method: app.stats before and after the idle period: frames drawn (minus the one the second app.stats request wakes), wake reasons, and process CPU time of all threads (watcher included)

launch.method: launch_to_present: the app's own figure (first line of run() to the first presented frame, STRATA_READY_FILE). spawn_to_ready: process spawn to the ready file, so exec, dyld and main count too. warm: same binary and HOME as an unmeasured first launch. cold-ish: the binary copied to a new path and an empty HOME each run (first-run work of a new binary: code-signature checks, dyld and Metal shader caches miss); the disk cache is warm (no purge without root). The window opens in front, as for a person.

strata.method: A new process with an empty HOME per run. first_lines: log.open_dialog sent → ui.wait reply for the first table row's element (answered on the frame that drew it). indexed: until log.files reports the file complete (polled every 2 ms). index_job: the app's own seconds for its open + index jobs (line index and per-chunk time/level summaries). search job_ms: the app's seconds for the search or filter job over the whole indexed file (count = the toolbar's match counter or the status bar's shown lines). Memory: macOS physical footprint from app.stats and RSS from ps; peak = the OS's lifetime peak footprint.

scroll.method: ui.scroll over the table (a wheel event at its center, one per request, reversing halfway); app.stats reset before each kind, then frame_cpu (eframe's whole-frame CPU on the UI thread, painting included) and ui (the runtime's view code) percentiles over the frames of the scroll
